# Third-Party Licenses

Branvio is licensed under `MIT OR Apache-2.0` (see `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`).
This file reproduces the license texts, copyright notices and NOTICE files of the
third-party code compiled into the Branvio binary, as required by those licenses
for binary distribution. The inventory and license notes are in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
The crate set is the union over all target platforms.

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_third_party_notices.py; do not edit by hand. -->

## Contents

1. Bundled native (C/C++) libraries
2. Rust crates: license, copyright and NOTICE files (deduplicated)
3. Rust crates that ship no license file (canonical license texts)
4. Design assets (not bundled in the current build)

## 1. Bundled native (C/C++) libraries

### AWS-LC (bundled C library via `aws-lc-sys`, used by rustls)

Crate: `aws-lc-sys` 0.47.0.

AWS-LC is Apache-2.0 / ISC with OpenSSL- and SSLeay-licensed portions; its LICENSE also lists the third-party code compiled into libcrypto (fiat-crypto, s2n-bignum, Jitter Entropy).

### libgit2 (bundled C library, statically linked via `git2` / `libgit2-sys`)

Crate: `libgit2-sys` 0.18.8+1.9.7.

libgit2 is GPL-2.0 *with the libgit2 linking exception*: linking it into a program and distributing the result under any license is permitted; modifications to libgit2 itself stay under its license. `COPYING` below is reproduced verbatim and also covers the bundled third-party code (zlib, PCRE2, wildmatch, SHA1DC, ntlmclient, llhttp, xdiff, the OpenSSL-licensed parts, and the LGPL-2.1 winhttp headers). The LGPL-2.1 winhttp import headers (`deps/winhttp`) are only used for MinGW builds; the MSVC Windows build links the system `winhttp.lib` from the Windows SDK. If a MinGW build is ever distributed, the LGPL-2.1 obligations for those headers apply (offer their source and allow relinking).

PCRE2 is a library of functions to support regular expressions whose syntax
and semantics are as close as possible to those of the Perl 5 language.

Releases 10.00 and above of PCRE2 are distributed under the terms of the "BSD"
licence, as specified below, with one exemption for certain binary
redistributions. The documentation for PCRE2, supplied in the "doc" directory,
is distributed under the same terms as the software itself. The data in the
testdata directory is not copyrighted and is in the public domain.

The basic library functions are written in C and are freestanding. Also
included in the distribution is a just-in-time compiler that can be used to
optimize pattern matching. This is an optional feature that can be omitted when
the library is built. The just-in-time compiler is separately licensed under the
"2-clause BSD" licence.
